SYNTHETIC FIXTURE. Halewater Commons Trust, Kelverton, the Marlpit ward, Dunmore Sixth Form College, St Aidan's Parish Hall, Priya Raval, Northgate Minibus Hire, the Second Chances course, the Wren Hill Foundation and the Neighbourhood Futures Fund do not exist, and no figure or date in the proposal is a fact about any real organisation. Every fact about the applicant in out-n06-B.md traces to an item in ledger-n06.json (6 named referents, one of each kind: Marlpit, Dunmore Sixth Form College, Second Chances, St Aidan's Parish Hall, Priya Raval, Northgate Minibus Hire). out-n06-B.md itself carries no synthetic-fixture header, following the out-n03-B.md precedent for this arm, because the task specifies the file must contain the finished proposal only so a critic can read it blind; the labelling is carried here and in every other file of the fixture.

WORD COUNTS, all deterministic, none from a model. wc -w on the whole file = 1520. The worker's own wordCount() (index.ts:563, strips |#*`> then counts alphanumeric tokens) = 1392. The donor counts only the five answers and explicitly excludes headings, the budget table and the declaration; counted that way the document is 1122 words (wc -w) / 1056 (worker wordCount) against the 1200 hard limit, i.e. compliant with 78 words to spare. The whole-document figure of 1392 still exceeds 1200, so contentViolations() would still report over_word_limit on the delivered file - see FAILURES below.

STAGES RUN (Draft tier, per pipeline-spec.md): analyze; org (NO model call - the fixture domain must not be crawled, so ledger-n06.json IS the org stage output; org.profile and org.voice_guide left null, so baseCtx segments 2 and 6 were absent); voice (skipped, no uploads); strategy (spec-effort attempt lost to the transport cap, then a retry, then 1 continuation); deterministic strategy selection (candidate 0, feasibility 88, distinctness clear; template id 1 problem_first, opening id 1 incident, per the spec's first-of-grant replay recipe); design + 1 continuation; gen:narrative + 1 continuation; generateValidated attempt-2 repair + 2 continuations (one discarded, see below); generateValidated attempt-3 length-only shorten + 1 continuation; validate.claim_ledger + 2 continuations; validate.review; validate.correction + 2 continuations; a further generateValidated attempt-2 repair on the corrected narrative + 1 continuation. check (skipped - nothing to compare against on a single replay); package/deliver (deterministic, not replayed).

FIDELITY DEVIATIONS, all forced and all recorded.
(1) The MCP transport hard-caps a single call at 60s. The spec's max_tokens (strategy 4500, design 6000, narrative 7000, correction 7000) could not be used. The strategy stage was attempted once at the spec's effort='high' with max_tokens 4500 and timed out with no response; that call is counted in `calls` and its input estimated at 4400 and completion at 4500 tokens because it very likely completed and was billed upstream. Cost excluding that lost call is $1.4046. Strategy and design therefore ran at effort='low' rather than the spec's 'high'.
(2) Eleven calls truncated on the token cap and were completed with the spec's own CONTINUATION_TURN (index.ts:154-167), but through a single-user-message transport the continuation cannot carry the original message array. Where the missing context mattered I reconstructed the prior turns inside the single message, labelled [EARLIER USER TURN] / [YOUR REPLY SO FAR] / [NEW USER TURN]. The damage is visible in two places. In the strategy stage the continuation abandoned the required schema and emitted `recommendation` instead of `ranking`/`ranking_reason`; jsonOf() parses it, and the worker's own fallback (index.ts:1473, ranking absent -> candidates.map((_,i)=>i)) then selects candidate 0, which is what I did. In the design stage the continuation abandoned the schema more severely, emitting `what_ends`, `assets_retained`, `future_funding`, `monitoring` and `assumptions`-as-bare-strings, and DROPPING `indicators`, `budget_envelope_usd`, `budget_drivers`, the typed `assumptions` and `logic_check` entirely, with `risks` and `assumptions` nested inside `project`. jsonOf() parses it and the missing keys pass silently, so the narrative was generated from a design object with no indicators and no budget envelope - which is why the budget was invented at narrative time rather than derived.
(3) One continuation call (call 10, 1158 in / 1500 out) was DISCARDED and re-run. My scaffolding for it listed the draft budget figures in the preamble, which invited the model to audit them; it emitted a meta-commentary block of arithmetic corrections with self-contradicting overhead figures. That contamination was mine, not the pipeline's, so it would have misrepresented the pipeline's output. The call is still counted in `calls` and in the token totals because it was billed. Call 11 is the faithful re-run.
(4) The spec's validate stage is deployed v26; the local worker source (which is ahead of v26) also runs properNounAudit() and contactAudit() in that stage. I followed the spec and did NOT run them.
(5) The claim-ledger call used 3 of the spec's 4 continuation hops and was still not complete; the tail claims (Q4 monitoring detail onward, most of the declaration) were not enumerated. The blocking classes it did return were complete enough to build the fixList.

FAILURES THE REPLAY EXPOSED, none of them fixed by hand.
(a) generateValidated never landed inside the word limit. Attempt 1 was 1611 (worker wordCount) against 1200; attempt-2 repair produced 1420; attempt-3 length-only shorten, told explicitly to cut to 936, produced 1394 - a 26-word cut against a 458-word instruction. On the real worker gen:narrative would therefore have thrown `content validation failed: over_word_limit` and the order would have died silently: sendEmail appears only in the deliver stage, so there is no failure notification. I continued the replay past that point, as the n03-B run did, in order to produce a deliverable.
(b) The validate correction pass made the document LONGER, 1394 -> 1493, despite the LENGTH clause instructing that the corrected version must not be longer than the current draft. A further generateValidated repair brought it to 1392.
(c) The deterministic consistency checker passed a budget that does not add up. The nine direct-cost lines sum to GBP 53,885; the table states a subtotal of 55,385, overstating direct costs by 1,500, and the 8 per cent overhead line (4,431) and total (59,816) are both computed from the wrong subtotal. consistencyFindings() never sums anything, so it reported nothing. The validate.review call CAUGHT it, in its own words, as the second-worst finding - but the tier is Draft, and reviewer findings enter the fixList only for competitive/full (index.ts fixList item 4), so the correction pass was never told about it and the error is in the delivered file. This is exactly the P1 defect recorded in CLAUDE.md, reproduced end to end.
(d) The grounding correction cost a named referent. The claim ledger classified the ledger's GBP 40 hall rate and GBP 95 minibus rate as `stale` (evidenced only to the year ending March 2025) and the correction removed the vendor's name with the price: `Northgate Minibus Hire` appears 0 times in the delivered file, so 5 of the ledger's 6 named referents survive. Counts in out-n06-B.md: Marlpit 10, Dunmore Sixth Form College 4, St Aidan's 3, Second Chances 2, Priya Raval 2, Northgate Minibus Hire 0.
(e) The correction pass added a sentence answering the one mandatory requirement the review call scored `missing` ("This application will be submitted before 17:00 GMT on Friday 27 November 2026"); the generateValidated repair that followed then deleted it again. The delivered file does not state the submission deadline.
(f) The opening device the strategy stage reserved was `incident` - "a dated, real event that makes the problem concrete". The ledger contains no incident and FACT_RULES forbids inventing one, so the narrative opens on the donor's Q1 heading and a constitution date. The reserved opening device was, in effect, unusable against this ledger.
(g) The design's `partnerships` marked Dunmore Sixth Form College, St Aidan's Parish Hall and Northgate Minibus Hire as `evidence_based`, which the ledger supports as a referral route, a hire and a purchase - but not as agreements. The claim ledger then flagged the narrative's bilateral agreement as unsupported and the correction recast it as "to be negotiated", which is the right outcome reached two stages late.

COST BASIS. anthropic/claude-opus-5 priced at $5/M input and $25/M output; that rate reproduces meta-n03-B.json's recorded $1.1972 from its recorded 67020/34485 tokens exactly. Every token figure here except the lost strategy call is the exact usage the API reported.
